The presence of contrast enhancement with a thick margin further points towards an IDH-wildtype glioma. Features such as central necrosis (NCR Volume (mL) > 0), a thick enhancing margin, significant mass effect, and deep infiltrative behavior (Deep WM invasion, Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion) are characteristic of high-grade astrocytomas, not oligodendrogliomas. The deep midline location involving the thalamus and corpus callosum is also atypical for oligodendroglioma. While there is cortical involvement, which can be seen in oligodendrogliomas, this is a non-specific finding and is heavily outweighed by the features arguing against co-deletion.

This single feature is sufficient for a high-confidence prediction. The diagnosis is further corroborated by other features of high-grade malignancy, including contrast enhancement (ET Volume (mL) of 4.017), a thick enhancing margin, extensive vasogenic edema (ED Volume (mL) of 104.855), and significant mass effect (max_shift_mm of 12.0). overall_comment: The imaging findings are highly characteristic of a glioblastoma. The key feature is the presence of central necrosis, which, in combination with contrast enhancement, extensive edema, and significant mass effect, strongly indicates a WHO grade 4 tumor. The deep midline location and infiltrative features are classic for an IDH-wildtype glioma. All individual predictions are consistent with the integrated diagnosis of Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4.
